best_for: Developers who want a free, open-source local container and Kubernetes setup on Windows or Mac, with their choice of containerd or Docker and a Kubernetes version they pick.

points.title: Choose your container engine
points.text: Run containerd with the nerdctl command, or dockerd with the familiar docker command. Both come bundled, so you can build and run images without another tool.

points.title: Pin a Kubernetes version
points.text: You pick the Kubernetes version in Preferences and can move between versions to test how an upgrade affects your workloads before it reaches a real cluster.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Rancher Desktop is open source under the Apache 2.0 license, from SUSE. Help comes from the community Slack channel and GitHub issues.

points.title: Plan for 8 GB of memory
points.text: The docs recommend 8 GB of RAM, 4 CPUs, hardware virtualization and a steady internet connection on every platform.

points.title: Windows 11 and WSL first
points.text: Windows needs Windows 11, Home included, or Server 2025, with WSL installed before you run the setup. Admin rights are only needed for an optional service that exposes containers beyond 127.0.0.1. The MSI listed here installs for all users.

points.title: Mac needs macOS 13
points.text: There are separate Intel and Apple silicon disk images for macOS 13 or later. The project says the Homebrew package is not maintained by its team.

points.title: No Linux listing here
points.text: The project ships .deb, .rpm and AppImage builds from its own repositories, but this site lists only Windows and macOS. The Windows listing keeps 47 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
